summary: Józef Turczyński held posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music (~1915–1919) and the Chopin University of Music (~1920–1939), where he taught Constantin Régamey.

Linguist József Budenz studied under Theodor Benfey and at the universities of Marburg and Göttingen. He served as librarian at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (1861) and as full professor of Altaic comparative linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).

Working in Japanology and Buddhist studies, Jörg B. Quenzer has held posts at the University of Hamburg and as an editorial board member and editor for Studies in Manuscript Cultures (both attested 2016).

Jörg Heimbel, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at Tibet University and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Dorji Wangchuk and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He became a Tibetan lecturer at Hamburg (attested 2019).
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Jörg Plassen has served as a professor at Geumgang University and Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).

Jørn Borup specialized in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University (~1998–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, and served there as associate professor from ~2008 to 2023.

Indologist Jürgen Hanneder studied at Munich, Bochum, Bonn, and Marburg (PhD ~1991–1996 under Michael Hahn). He worked at Bonn and Halle, and in 2007 succeeded Hahn as professor at the University of Marburg.
Working in Indology and history and archaeology, Jürgen Neuß studied under Harry Falk and completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2007.

Historian of science and philosopher Jürgen Renn studied at the Free University of Berlin, Rome, and TU Berlin. He held posts at Boston University, became Director at the MPI for the History of Science (1994), and Director at MPI-GEA (2022).

Historian and Indologist K. A. Nilakanta Sastri studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He held posts at Annamalai University, the University of Mysore, and served as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Madras (~1929–1946).

Specialist in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy K. A. Subramania Iyer studied at London and Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Lionel David Barnett. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Lucknow (1921–1960) and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1960–1961).
Indology scholar K. Ammini Amma was attested as a research student at the University of Madras in 1940 and 1971.
Indologist K. Balasubramania Iyer served as managing editor of the Journal of Oriental Research, Madras, and as secretary at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945).
Working in linguistics and Indology, K. Kanapathypillai studied at Hartley College and the University of London (~1934–1936), and later taught Alvappillai Veluppillai.

Indologist and linguist K. Kunjunni Raja completed PhDs at Madras under C. Kunhan Raja and London under John Brough. He served as Professor and Head of Sanskrit at the University of Madras from 1951, succeeding V. Raghavan in 1969.

Buddhist studies scholar K. L. Dhammajoti studied at the University of Kelaniya under Yin Shun and Y. Karunadasa. He taught at Kelaniya, held leadership posts at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1989–2003), and worked at HKU (~2004–2014).

Indologist K. Madhava Krishna Sarma was a research student under C. Kunhan Raja. He was affiliated with the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940, 1971) and served as curator at the Anup Sanskrit Library (attested 1946).
Indologist and linguist K. Meenakshi earned a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under M. A. Mehendale, and was later affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).
Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, K. Munirathnam studied under N. S. Ramachandra Murthy and served as Director (Epigraphy) I/c at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2013–2018).

Scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy K. N. Jayatilleke studied under O. H. de A. Wijesekera, and under Ludwig Wittgenstein at Cambridge (1945–1948). He later served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon (~1951–1963).
